raw_text:
Here’s the complete 12-week postpartum return plan summary for your 33-year-old client, starting at 4 weeks post uncomplicated C-section. It integrates phases, weekly structure, sessions, strength, core, cardio, and breastfeeding-supportive nutrition. All progressions hinge on symptom-free movement: no pain, incision pulling, increased bleeding, doming/coning, pelvic heaviness/pressure, or leaking. If any appear, regress to the prior week and/or consult her provider. Obtain OB clearance for “exercise” at 6 weeks before initiating direct core work and structured strength.

Global structure
- Frequency: 4–5 training days/week + 2 recovery/light days.
- Session types: Strength (total-body), Core (tiered), Cardio (steady and intervals), Mobility/breath.
- Intensity: RPE 2–3 early; RPE 4–7 by Weeks 8–12 on main lifts/cardio peaks.
- Equipment: Yoga mat; optional chair/wall; later add backpack/water jugs/bands if ready.

PHASE 1 (Weeks 1–2 here = postpartum weeks 4–6): Heal, activate, easy walks
Goals: Support healing; restore breath, pelvic floor and deep core control; gentle mobility; short, flat walks. No direct abs yet, no lifting beyond infant/household items.

Week 1
- Breath/pelvic floor (daily, 8–10 min): 360° breathing 5 x 5; gentle pelvic floor lifts 2 x 8 (3s lift/3s relax); heel slides 1–2 x 6/side; supine tiny marches 1 x 6/side.
- Mobility (5–8 min): Small cat-cow 1–2 x 6; sidelying thoracic rotations 1 x 6/side; ankle pumps 1 x 10.
- Cardio: 2–3 walks, 10–15 min, RPE 2–3.
- Coaching: Posture stacked; stop with any incision pulling or increased bleeding.

Week 2
- Breath/core: 360 breathing 5 x 5; quick flicks 2 x 6; longer holds 2 x 5 (4–5s); dead bug arms-only 2 x 6/side; heel slides or toe taps tiny 2 x 6/side.
- Mobility: Add seated lat/chest opener, 20–30s holds.
- Cardio: 3 walks, 15–20 min, RPE 2–3.

Week 3 (pre 6-week check; if not yet cleared, stay at Week 2)
- Breath/core: As above; progress to controlled supine marching 2 x 8/side; dead bug arms + heel slide 2 x 6/side.
- Mobility: Gentle hip flexor release 20s/side if comfortable.
- Cardio: 20–25 min, 3–4 days, easy.

PHASE 2 (Weeks 4–5 here = postpartum weeks 6–8): Foundational strength and direct core (after OB clearance)
Goals: Introduce simple patterns; diastasis-safe core; extend walks.

Week 4 (PP week 7)
- Strength 2–3x/wk (20–25 min, RPE 3–4): Sit-to-stand 3 x 8; wall push-up 3 x 8; hip hinge drill 3 x 8; bridge (feet close) 3 x 8 with 2–3s exhale lift; quadruped rocking 2 x 8.
- Core 10 min: Dead bug arms + toe tap 2 x 6/side; side-lying clams 2 x 10/side; tall-kneel hands-press anti-rotation holds 2 x 5 x 5s.
- Cardio: 25–30 min walk, 3–4 days.

Week 5 (PP week 8)
- Strength 2–3x/wk (25–30 min, RPE 4–5): Sit-to-stand 3 x 10 (1s pause); elevated push-up 3 x 8–10; hip hinge mini good-morning 3 x 10; bridge with 3–5s hold 3 x 8; split-stance weight shift 2 x 8/side.
- Core: Dead bug contralateral short-range 3 x 5/side; clams 3 x 10/side; bird dog arms-only 2 x 6/side.
- Cardio: 30–35 min, 3–4 days; optionally 2 x 1-min brisk intervals.

PHASE 3 (Weeks 6–9 here = postpartum weeks 8–12): Capacity and intensity build (pushed per your request)
Goals: Raise RPE to 5–7 on main lifts by set’s end; add sets, tempo, unilateral; structured intervals. Add light loading (backpack/jugs/bands) only if symptom-free.

Week 6 (PP week 9) – Build
- Strength 3x/wk (30–35 min, RPE 5–6):
  - Day A: Squat to target tempo 3-1-1 4 x 8–10; counter push-up 4 x 6–10; bridge 3 x 10–12; split squat shallow 3 x 6–8/side; core: dead bug full 3 x 5/side; side plank (knees) 3 x 20–25s/side. Optional 6-min alternating 30s step-ups/30s bridge hold.
  - Day B: Good-morning tempo 3-1-1 4 x 8–10; single-arm row (band/jug or isometric squeeze) 3–4 x 8–12/side; reverse lunge supported 3 x 6–8/side; tall/half-kneel press-out 3 x 8 with 3s holds; core: bird dog 3 x 6–8/side; bear rock-backs knees down 2 x 6–8.
  - Day C: Single-leg sit-to-stand assist 3 x 6/side; hip bridge march 3 x 10/side; incline push-up 3 x 8–12; lateral step to balance 3 x 8/side; core: Pallof or hands-press 3 x 8 with 3s holds; dead bug slow 3 x 4/side.
- Cardio: 35–40 min steady 1–2x; Intervals: 5-min warm-up; 6–7 x 1-min brisk / 90s–2-min easy; 5-min cool-down.

Week 7 (PP week 10) – Intensify
- Strength 3x/wk (RPE 6–7):
  - Day A: Squat lower target or goblet with backpack 4 x 8; counter push-up 3s eccentric 4 x 6–8; bridge march 3 x 10/side; split squat to target 3 x 8/side; core: side plank (knees, top leg straight) 3 x 20–30s/side; dead bug 3 x 5–6/side. EMOM 6–8 min: Min1 10 air squats; Min2 8 counter push-ups.
  - Day B: Good-morning (light load if ready) 4 x 8–10; single-arm row 4 x 8–12/side; reverse lunge to balance 3 x 8/side; half-kneel anti-rotation 3 x 8 with 3s holds; core: bear hover 3 x 8–12s (or extend bird dog).
  - Day C: Single-leg bridge 3 x 8–10/side; lateral step-down low target 3 x 6–8/side; incline push-up lower surface 4 x 8–12; hinge isometric hold 3 x 10; core: Pallof 3 x 8; side plank 2 x 25–30s/side.
- Cardio: 40–45 min steady; Intervals: 6 x 90s brisk / 90s easy.

Week 8 (PP week 11) – Peak of Phase 3
- Strength 3x/wk:
  - Day A: Goblet squat 4 x 8–10; push-up progression 4 x 8–12; loaded bridge 3 x 10–12; loaded split squat 3 x 8/side; core: dead bug 3-1-3 3 x 5/side; side plank knees or short‑lever Copenhagen 3 x 20–25s/side. Finisher 7–8 min: 40s high march + 20s wall sit x 7–8.
  - Day B: Good-morning loaded 4 x 8–10; single-arm row loaded 4 x 8–12/side; single-leg RDL pattern 3 x 6–8/side; half-kneel press-out 3 x 8 with 3s holds; core: bear hover 3 x 12–15s (or quadruped reaches).
  - Day C: Single-leg sit-to-stand assist 3 x 8/side; reverse lunge to balance 3 x 8/side; incline push-up 3 x 10–12; lateral step to balance 3 x 8/side; core: dead bug thigh-press 2 x 5/side; Pallof 3 x 8.
- Cardio: One 45–50 min steady; Intervals: 8 x 75–90s brisk / 75–90s easy.

PHASE 4 (Weeks 10–12 here = postpartum weeks 12–15): Strong finish and consolidation
Goals: Solid strength endurance and stable core under moderate load; confident brisk walking capacity. No HIIT yet; consider low-impact HIIT on-ramp only after 12–16 weeks if fully symptom-free and ideally after pelvic floor PT clearance.

Week 9 (PP week 12)
- Strength 3x/wk (RPE 6–7):
  - Day A: Goblet squat 4 x 8–10 (3s down); push-up lower incline or controlled knees 4 x 8–10; hip thrust/bridge loaded 4 x 8–12; split squat loaded 3 x 8/side; core: bear hover 3 x 12–20s; side plank progression 3 x 25–30s/side; Pallof 3 x 8 with 3s holds. EMOM 6 min: 10–12 goblet squats, then 8–10 counter push-ups alternating minutes.
  - Day B: Good-morning loaded 4 x 8–10; single-arm row 4 x 10–12/side; single-leg RDL pattern 3 x 8/side; reverse lunge to balance 3 x 8/side; core: dead bug slow 3 x 5–6/side; anti-rotation 3 x 8 with 3s holds.
- Cardio: 45–50 min steady; Intervals: 10 x 60s brisk / 60s easy.

Week 10 (PP week 13)
- Strength Day 1 (RPE 6–7): Goblet squat 4 x 8; push-up 4 x 8–10 (3s eccentric); bridge/hip thrust 3 x 10–12; split squat 3 x 8/side; core: bear hover or incline plank 3 x 15–25s; side plank 3 x 25–30s/side.
- Strength Day 2 (RPE 6–7): Good-morning 4 x 8–10; single-arm row 4 x 10–12/side; single-leg RDL 3 x 8/side; reverse lunge 3 x 8/side; core: dead bug thigh-press 3 x 5/side; Pallof 3 x 8 with 3s holds.
- Total-body circuit (8–10 min, RPE 6): 3 rounds—40s goblet squat; 20s rest; 40s counter push-ups; 20s; 40s loaded bridge; 20s; 40s band/jug rows; 60s rest.
- Cardio: 45–50 min steady; Intervals: 6 x 2-min brisk / 2-min easy.

Week 11 (PP week 14)
- Strength 3x/wk (RPE 6–7): Squat 4 x 10; push-up lower incline or more reps 4 x 8–12; hinge tempo 3-1-1 3 x 12; reverse lunge to balance 3 x 8/side; lateral step to curtsy reach small 3 x 6–8/side.
- Core: Dead bug with thigh press 3 x 6/side; bear shoulder taps only if rock-solid 2 x 6/side; side plank with top leg lift if ready 2 x 8/side.
- Cardio: 45–50 min steady; Intervals: 10 x 60s brisk / 60–90s easy.

Week 12 (PP week 15) – Performance week (feel strong, not wrecked)
- Strength: 2 strength sessions (as Week 10 Day 1 and Day 2) + 1 total-body circuit (8–10 min at RPE 6).
- Core finisher (choose 2): Dead bug slow x 6/side; side plank knees or short‑lever Copenhagen x 15–20s/side; bear hover x 15–20s.
- Cardio: One 45–50 min steady walk; One interval 6 x 2-min brisk / 2-min easy.
- Post-program: If symptom-free, consider starting low-impact HIIT on-ramp after Week 12–16 and/or begin adding modest external loads (bands/dumbbells).

Core progression tiers summary (when to add “abs”)
- Tier 0 (Weeks 4–6 PP): Activation only—breath, PF, heel slides, tiny marches.
- Tier 1 (post 6-week clearance): Diastasis-safe direct core—dead bug short-range, modified side plank, bird dog small, anti-rotation.
- Tier 2 (Weeks 8–12 PP): Full dead bug, side plank progressions, bear rock-backs knees down, Pallof presses.
- Tier 3 (≥12 weeks PP if symptom-free): Bear hover, incline planks; progress slowly. Traditional high-pressure abs much later and only if cleared.

Breastfeeding-supportive nutrition (ongoing through all phases)
- Energy: +300–500 kcal/day over maintenance; adjust to appetite, recovery, weight trends, and milk supply. Keep early weeks out of deficit.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; anchor 20–35 g per meal + protein-forward snacks.
- Carbs: 45–60% calories from mostly whole, fiber-rich sources to support training and milk.
- Fats: 25–35% calories; include omega-3s (DHA/EPA).
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; +300–500 ml around sessions; consider electrolytes.
- Micronutrients: Continue OB-recommended prenatal/postnatal. Emphasize iron, iodine, calcium, choline, vitamin D, B12 (if vegetarian), DHA 300–600 mg/day.
- Easy meal template: Each meal = protein + colorful veg/fruit + smart carbs + healthy fat. 1–2 snacks/day (protein + carb or fat).

Below is a conservative, OB‑clearance–aligned 12‑week postpartum return plan for a 33‑year‑old client four weeks post uncomplicated C‑section. It emphasizes healing, breath, pelvic floor and deep core reactivation, gradual walking volume, and progressive total‑body strength using only a yoga mat. No direct abdominal loading, planks, or heavy lifting until after the six‑week check; even after, core work progresses thoughtfully with diastasis‑safe options. Encourage her to stop any movement that causes pain, pulling at the incision, doming/bulging of the midline, increased pelvic pressure, urinary leaking, or bleeding increase. If any red flags occur, she should stop and consult her provider.

Structure
- Frequency: 4–5 days/week (short sessions), with at least 2 full rest or light‑activity days weekly.
- Session types: Breath/pelvic floor + mobility; walking; gentle strength (bodyweight); progressive core reconditioning.
- Intensity: RPE 2–6 across phases. Maintain nasal/comfortable conversational pace for cardio.
- Progression gates: Advance only if no pain, no incision pulling, no doming/coning, no increased bleeding, and good control of breath/pelvic floor.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2 here = postpartum weeks 4–6): Healing support, breath, pelvic floor engagement, posture, very gentle mobility, easy walks. No direct abs, no lifting beyond infant/household light loads.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 3–4 here = postpartum weeks 6–8): After 6‑week check and clearance for “exercise,” introduce foundational strength patterns and gentle, direct core reconditioning with diastasis‑safe choices.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 5–8 = postpartum weeks 8–12): Build volume and light intensity, add time under tension, unilateral stability, gentle cardio intervals, and progress core challenge.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 9–12 = postpartum weeks 12–16): Return to fuller strength training patterns (still bodyweight), moderate RPE, longer walks/intervals, and more dynamic but controlled core work.

General coaching points
- Breath: 360° diaphragmatic breathing. Inhale to expand ribcage and back; exhale to gently engage pelvic floor (lift) and lower abs (zip up) without bracing.
- Pelvic floor: Gentle submaximal contractions (30–50% effort) coordinated with breath; fully relax between reps.
- Posture: Stacked ribs over pelvis, soft knees, long spine, avoid rib flare.
- Incision care: No positions that pull on the scar; avoid prone and deep backbends early on. Support abdomen with hands/pillow during cough/sneeze.

  - Side plank modified with top leg straight: 3 x 15–20s/side
  - Seated anti-rotation (hands together) 5s: 2 x 6
- Walking/Cardio:
  - 40 min steady once; Intervals: 8 x 1-min brisk / 2-min easy.

PHASE 4: Weeks 10–12 here (PP weeks 12–16)
Goals: Solidify strength endurance, stable core under load, prepare for transition to external resistance and fuller training.

Week 9 (PP week 12)
- Strength (3x/week, RPE 5–6):
  - Squat to target (deeper if tolerated): 4 x 8
  - Incline push-up (low bench/couch back): 4 x 6–10
  - Hip hinge to long lever good morning (hands behind head): 3 x 10
  - Single-leg bridge: 3 x 8/side
  - Lateral step to balance (side step, hold 2s): 3 x 8/side
- Core:
  - Dead bug slow tempo 3-1-3: 3 x 5/side
  - Copenhagen side plank (short lever, knee on floor) or continue modified side plank: 3 x 12–15s/side
  - Bear hover introduction (knees under hips, hover 1–2 inches, only if no doming/leakage): 3 x 10s; otherwise quadruped holds.
- Cardio:
  - 40–45 min steady; Intervals: 6 x 90s brisk / 2 min easy.

Week 10 (PP week 13)
- Strength (3x/week):
  - Split squat full ROM as tolerated: 3 x 8/side
  - Incline push-up or kneeling floor push-up (only if no pressure symptoms): 4 x 6–8
  - Hip hinge to isometric row squeeze: 3 x 12
  - Bridge march slow tempo: 3 x 10/side
  - Single-leg RDL pattern without load (reach to wall): 3 x 6/side
- Core:
  - Dead bug or hollow‑prep (supine, knees bent, posterior pelvic tilt) 10–15s: 3 x 3
  - Bear hover 3 x 10–15s or quadruped opposite reaches: 3 x 6/side
  - Side plank forearm, knees bent: 3 x 25–30s/side
- Cardio:
  - 45 min steady or 20–30 min stroller hill walk if available; Intervals: 8 x 60–75s brisk / 90–120s easy.

- Strength (3x/week, RPE 6):
  - Squat 4 x 10
  - Push-up progression: lower incline or more reps 4 x 8–12
  - Hip hinge tempo 3-1-1 3 x 12
  - Reverse lunge to balance 3 x 8/side
  - Lateral step to curtsy reach (small) 3 x 6–8/side

  - Dead bug contralateral with band-thigh press (palms into thighs) 3 x 6/side
  - Bear shoulder taps (only if rock-solid, tiny taps): 2 x 6/side
  - Side plank with top leg lift (if ready) 2 x 8/side
- Cardio:
  - 45 min steady; Intervals: 10 x 60s brisk / 60–90s easy.

- Strength (3x/week):
  - Circuit A x 3 rounds (RPE 6): Squat x12; Counter push-up x10–12; Hip hinge x12; Single-leg bridge x10/side; Split squat x8/side. 60–75s rest between rounds.
- Core finisher (choose 2):
  - Dead bug slow x 6/side
  - Side plank knees x 30s/side or short-lever Copenhagen x 15s/side
  - Bear hover x 15–20s
- Cardio:
  - One 45–50 min steady walk; One interval session: 6 x 2-min brisk / 2-min easy.

- Watch for coning/doming along midline during core moves. If present, regress range or selection.
- Pelvic floor: Any heaviness, pressure, pain, or leaking warrants regression and/or referral to a pelvic floor physical therapist.
- Incision: Any redness, heat, discharge, or increasing pain—cease and seek medical guidance.

- Sleep: Prioritize naps and consistent bed/wake windows where possible.
- Walking shoes: Supportive footwear to reduce impact fatigue.
- Hydration: Aim ~2–3 L/day; add 500–700 ml if breastfeeding and as thirst dictates.

Big rocks
- Energy: Start with +300–500 kcal/day above estimated maintenance; adjust to appetite, recovery, and milk supply. If weight loss is desired later, keep losses slow (0.25–0.5 kg/week max) and ensure supply remains stable.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (e.g., 90–120 g/day for a 60 kg woman). Anchor 20–35 g protein per meal + 10–20 g in snacks.
- Carbohydrates: 45–60% of calories; emphasize whole, fiber‑rich sources to support energy and milk production.
- Fats: 25–35% of calories; include omega‑3s (DHA/EPA), monounsaturated fats, and some saturated fat from quality sources.
- Hydration: Aim 2.5–3.5 L fluids/day, more in heat/exercise; include electrolytes if sweating. Use thirst and urine color (pale straw) as guides.
- Micronutrients: Emphasize iron, iodine, calcium, choline, vitamin D, B12 (if vegetarian), and DHA. Continue OB-recommended prenatal/postnatal vitamins; add a separate DHA (300–600 mg/day) if not included.

Meal structure template
- 3 meals + 1–2 snacks. Each meal: protein + colorful veg/fruit + smart carbs + healthy fat. Each snack: protein-forward + carb or fat.
- Example portion targets per meal:
  - Protein: 1–2 palms (20–35 g)
  - Carbs: 1–2 cupped hands (30–60 g), more near/between feeds if energy dips
  - Veg/fruit: 1–2 fists
  - Fats: 1–2 thumbs (10–20 g)

Sample 1‑day menus (mix and match)
- Day A
  - Breakfast: Greek yogurt (200 g) + oats (1/2 cup dry) + blueberries + chia (1 tbsp) + honey; coffee/tea + water.
  - Snack: Apple + cheddar (40 g) or soy yogurt (protein-fortified).
  - Lunch: Whole‑grain wrap with rotisserie chicken or chickpeas, avocado, spinach, tomato; side carrots + hummus.
  - Snack (night feed friendly): Cottage cheese (150–200 g) with pineapple or a protein smoothie (milk/soy milk, banana, peanut butter, spinach).
  - Dinner: Salmon (120–150 g) or tofu, quinoa/brown rice, roasted veg (broccoli, peppers), olive oil drizzle.
- Day B
  - Breakfast: Eggs (2–3) scrambled with spinach + whole‑grain toast + orange.
  - Snack: Trail mix (nuts/seeds + dried fruit) or roasted edamame.
  - Lunch: Lentil soup + whole‑grain pita + side salad with olive oil/lemon.
  - Snack: Whole‑milk kefir or skyr + granola.
  - Dinner: Lean beef or tempeh taco bowls: rice, black beans, veggies, salsa, cheese/avocado.

Quick breastfeeding snacks
- String cheese + crackers; tuna pouch + whole‑grain crackers; hummus + veg; hard‑boiled eggs; nut butter on toast; edamame; cottage cheese + fruit; smoothie packs; oatmeal with milk and flax.

Hydration plan
- Keep a 700–1000 ml bottle at hand; aim for 1 bottle by mid‑morning, 1 by mid‑afternoon, and 1 by evening; add 300–500 ml around workouts/walks.
- Include 1–2 electrolyte servings/day if sweating or in hot weather. Herbal teas and milk count; limit caffeinated coffee/tea to ~200–300 mg caffeine/day if baby is sensitive.

Key nutrients and easy food sources
- DHA/EPA: Salmon, sardines, trout; DHA-fortified eggs; algae oil supplement for vegetarians (300–600 mg/day).
- Choline (aim ~450–550 mg/day): Eggs (1 egg ~150 mg), beef, chicken, soy, quinoa; consider choline bitartrate if intake is low.
- Iodine (220–290 mcg/day): Iodized salt, dairy, eggs, seafood; prenatal usually covers.
- Iron (9–10 mg/day in lactation; higher if low ferritin): Lean red meat, legumes, fortified cereals; pair with vitamin C foods; keep supplementation per OB.
- Calcium (1000 mg/day): Dairy, fortified plant milks, tofu set with calcium, leafy greens, canned fish with bones.
- Vitamin D: 600–2000 IU/day depending on labs/sun; often supplement per provider.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day from oats, legumes, fruit, veg, flax/chia; increase gradually with fluids to minimize GI discomfort.

Support for GI comfort and incision recovery
- Prioritize easy‑to‑digest meals in first weeks; chew well, avoid large high‑fat meals right before sleep.
- To reduce constipation/straining: daily oats or prunes, kiwi, leafy greens, legumes, flax/chia (1 tbsp), plus adequate fluids.
- If gas/bloating: trial smaller, more frequent meals; soak/rinse legumes; consider lactose‑free dairy or low‑FODMAP swaps short‑term if sensitive.

Feeding‑friendly timing
- Small snack 30–60 min before longer walks or strength (e.g., yogurt + fruit or toast + nut butter).
- Post‑session: protein 20–30 g + carbs 30–60 g within 1–2 hours (e.g., smoothie or sandwich) to support recovery and milk supply.
- Night feeds: Keep shelf‑stable or ready‑to‑eat options bedside (trail mix, bars with 10–20 g protein, shelf‑stable milk).

Simple 2‑week rotating grocery list
- Proteins: Eggs, Greek yogurt/skyr or soy yogurt, cottage cheese/kefir, milk/soy milk, chicken thighs/breast, canned tuna/salmon, lean beef/turkey, tofu/tempeh, lentils/beans, edamame, protein powder (whey or soy/pea).
- Carbs: Oats, whole‑grain bread/wraps, brown rice/quinoa, potatoes, pasta, tortillas, granola, crackers.
- Produce: Berries, bananas, apples/oranges, leafy greens, broccoli, peppers, carrots, onions, tomatoes, avocado, frozen veg medleys.
- Fats: Olive oil, avocado oil, nuts (almonds/walnuts), seeds (chia/flax/pumpkin), nut butters, olives.
- Extras: Iodized salt, spices, lemon, salsa, dark chocolate, electrolyte packets, prenatal/postnatal vitamin, DHA/algae oil if needed.

Safe weight management while breastfeeding
- First 6–8 weeks: prioritize supply and recovery; avoid intentional deficits.
- After 8–12 weeks, if supply is solid and energy is good: a modest calorie deficit (200–300 kcal/day) can support slow fat loss. Maintain protein at the higher end, keep hydration high, and monitor supply, energy, mood, and baby’s growth. If supply dips, return to maintenance.

Foods to limit/monitor
- Alcohol: If drinking, follow “pump and dump” is not necessary with moderate intake; instead, time feeds. A standard drink generally clears in 2–3 hours; use a reliable alcohol and breastfeeding guideline/app. When in doubt, wait.
- High‑mercury fish (limit swordfish, king mackerel); choose low‑mercury options (salmon, sardines, trout).
- Excess caffeine (>300 mg) if infant is jittery or sleep‑affected.
- Any personal allergens or infant sensitivities; keep a simple food/symptom log if suspecting reactions.

Supplements (confirm with OB)
- Continue prenatal/postnatal multivitamin.
- Vitamin D3 per labs (often 1000–2000 IU/day).
- DHA 300–600 mg/day if diet is low in fatty fish.
- Iron only if indicated by labs.
- Magnesium glycinate 100–200 mg at night may support sleep/regularity if approved.

Red flags and when to adjust
- Sudden milk supply drop, significant fatigue, dizziness, or rapid weight change: increase calories/fluids and consult provider or lactation consultant.
- Persistent GI distress, constipation, or incision discomfort: adjust fiber, hydration, and meal size; seek medical guidance if unresolved.

This plan keeps choices simple, breastfeeding‑supportive, and flexible around newborn life. Pair it with the training program by anchoring protein at each meal, hydrating consistently, and using easy snacks to bridge long stretches between feeds.

Since she currently has only a yoga mat, I’ve included no-equipment progressions first, then show how to add load with common household items (backpack, water jugs) and, if desired, basic gear (mini-bands, long loop band, a pair of dumbbells). Use the readiness gates: no pain, no doming/coning, no pelvic pressure/leaking, no incision pulling.

How to use
- Keep existing session structure, swap the listed movements for the progressed version when she meets the readiness gates, or add the “Load Option” column once she’s symptom-free at current step.
- Intensity target: RPE 4–6 most sets; last 2–3 reps should be challenging with clean form.

- Progress only one variable at a time: range of motion, reps/sets, then load, then tempo.

Phase-by-phase strength progression add-on

Weeks 4–6 postpartum (Weeks 1–3 of your plan: light only; bodyweight)
- Keep strength “pattern practice” and isometrics. No added load.
- Replace any movement that causes symptoms with an earlier, more supported variant.
- Focus: perfect sit-to-stand, hinge patterning, bridges, wall/counter push-ups, clams, bird dog arms-only.

Weeks 6–8 postpartum (Weeks 4–5 of your plan: foundational strength)
- Goal: Build volume and time under tension with bodyweight.
- Progressions by movement pattern:
  - Squat: Sit-to-stand → squat to target with 2–3s eccentric → add 1–2s pause at the bottom.
  - Hinge: Hip hinge drill → good-morning (hands behind head) → tempo 3–1–1.
  - Push: Wall push-up → counter push-up → slower eccentric (3s).
  - Bridge: Standard → bridge with 3–5s top hold → bridge march (controlled).

  - Main lifts: 3–4 sets of 8–12 reps (or 20–30s holds) at RPE 4–5.

Weeks 8–12 postpartum (Weeks 6–9 of your plan: introduce load and unilateral)
- Add household load if symptom-free with current bodyweight work.

  - Backpack load: Start 5–10 lb (2–5 kg). Add books/towels to reach RPE 6 by last reps.

- Pattern-specific progression and loading:
  - Squat: Goblet hold with backpack to chest.

    - 3 x 8–12/side.

  - Day A: Squat, Row, Bridge, Anti-rotation, Side plank
  - Day B: Hinge, Push-up, Split squat, Clamshell/hip abduction, Dead bug
  - Optional Day C: Repeat A or B with slightly lower volume (2 sets) or technique focus

- Frequency: 1 HIIT day/week only; keep 1–2 steady cardio days.

  - 5 min warm-up
  - 6–8 x 45s hard / 90s easy
  - 5 min cool-down

- Progressions
  - 10–12 x 45s hard / 60s easy (bike/elliptical or power walk)
  - 8–10 x 60s hard / 75–90s easy
  - Add gentle hills on walks if no pelvic response

  - Walk‑jog HIIT: 60s jog / 90s walk x 8–10 on flat terrain
  - Low box step‑ups to light hops later, one exercise per session, monitor symptoms during and 24–48 hours after

- Replace one weekly interval walk with the HIIT on‑ramp session; keep other cardio steady.

Core progression tiers summary (when to add “abs”)
- Tier 0 (Weeks 4–6 PP): Activation only—breath, PF, heel slides, tiny marches.
- Tier 1 (post 6-week clearance): Diastasis-safe direct core—dead bug short-range, modified side plank, bird dog small, anti-rotation.
- Tier 2 (Weeks 8–12 PP): Full dead bug, side plank progressions, bear rock-backs knees down, Pallof presses.
- Tier 3 (≥12 weeks PP if symptom-free): Bear hover, incline planks; progress slowly. Traditional high-pressure abs much later and only if cleared.

Breastfeeding-supportive nutrition (ongoing through all phases)
- Energy: +300–500 kcal/day over maintenance; adjust to appetite, recovery, weight trends, and milk supply. Keep early weeks out of deficit.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; anchor 20–35 g per meal + protein-forward snacks.
- Carbs: 45–60% calories from mostly whole, fiber-rich sources to support training and milk.
- Fats: 25–35% calories; include omega-3s (DHA/EPA).
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; +300–500 ml around sessions; consider electrolytes.
- Micronutrients: Continue OB-recommended prenatal/postnatal. Emphasize iron, iodine, calcium, choline, vitamin D, B12 (if vegetarian), DHA 300–600 mg/day.
- Easy meal template: Each meal = protein + colorful veg/fruit + smart carbs + healthy fat. 1–2 snacks/day (protein + carb or fat).
- Sample day: Yogurt + oats + berries + chia; wrap with chicken/chickpeas + avocado; salmon/tofu with quinoa and veg; snacks like cottage cheese + fruit, edamame, nut-butter toast.
- GI comfort: Oats/prunes/kiwi/flax + fluids for regularity; smaller meals if gassy; soak/rinse legumes.
- Weight management later: After 8–12 weeks, if supply solid and energy good, a small deficit (200–300 kcal) can reduce fat slowly. Monitor supply and recovery.

Cardio summary
- Build from 10–15 min easy walks to 45–50 min steady and structured brisk intervals by Week 12.
- Typical weekly mix from Week 5 onward: 2 steady walks + 1 interval session.
- No HIIT during Weeks 1–12. Consider low-impact HIIT on-ramp after Week 12–16 only if fully symptom-free and ideally after pelvic floor PT clearance.

Progression and monitoring
- Progress only one variable at a time (range → reps/sets → load → tempo).
- Keep last 2–3 reps challenging at target RPE with clean form.
- Red flags warrant regression and/or referral: pelvic heaviness, leaking, doming, back/pelvic pain, incision changes, increased bleeding, unusual fatigue.
- Recovery: 48 hours between like sessions; prioritize sleep opportunities; protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day and fluids.
